spec.title: theia PROP-002: Upstream identity and tree layout

status.comment: answers to TYPE-AREA-IDENTITY and TYPE-AREA-LAYOUT; facts 01, 02, 10; implemented in P5, and the second materialized directory of THEIA-APPLICATION-ROOT in P5-2

facts.THEIA-PIN-TAGS: Release tags match `v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+`; the rolling tag `next` is mutable and a pin resolver ignores it (`01-version-and-sha.md`, tag shape). A pin is `tag@sha@date` as everywhere; a pin on a master commit between tags is allowed and is written with the nearest reachable tag plus the sha (`v1.75.0@c8926e4d…`).
facts.THEIA-VERSION-SOURCE: The upstream version is read from `lerna.json` (`version`, fixed mode), not from the root `package.json`, which is the private `@theia/monorepo` at `0.0.0`; every `@theia/*` package carries the same literal version (`01`, "Where the version is written").
facts.THEIA-TREE-FINGERPRINT: `check-tree` fingerprints: root `package.json` named `@theia/monorepo` with `workspaces` covering `packages/*` and `dev-packages/*`; `lerna.json` with `npmClient: "npm"`; `packages/core/package.json` named `@theia/core` at the version of `lerna.json`; the anchor commit reachable from the pin (`01`, `02`).

facts.THEIA-OWN-ROOT: The own root is a workspace package directory: `typeConfig.ownRoot` defaults to `packages/<name>` and must match one of the workspace globs of the root `package.json` (`dev-packages/*`, `packages/*`, `examples/*`); the type refuses a root outside them (`CK-E-CONFIG`). A package under `packages/` is what the `theiaext` scripts, the generated tsconfig references and the `nls-extract` glob already cover (`10-downstream-own-package.md`, "Placement").
facts.THEIA-OWN-PACKAGE-SHAPE: The own root is an npm package with `theiaExtensions` (the ten entry kinds of `extension-package.ts:22-33`), `version` equal to the monorepo version, `dependencies` on the `@theia/*` packages it uses at the exact same version, the `theiaext` scripts (`lint`, `build`, `watch`, `clean`, `compile`, `test`) and `@theia/ext-scripts` as a dev dependency, its own `.eslintrc.js` and `tsconfig.json` (a package without them is not linted at all - `08`); the skeleton of `examples/api-provider-sample/package.json` is the reference (`10`, "The skeleton").
facts.THEIA-APPLICATION-ROOT: A product's application is a second directory the delta owns, `typeConfig.applicationRoot` (default `applications/<name>` or an `examples/*` slot), whose `package.json` is the overlay target of PROP-003. The type materializes both directories the way the `vscode` type materializes its own root: mirrored by content from the delta, excluded from the drift guard. **Implemented in P5-2** (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-LAYOUT`): the type answers `layout.ownRoots` with the own package (role `own`) and the application (role `application`), the delta keeps the second one under `delta/own-roots/application/`, and inside it **the pin is the boundary** - the files the pin ships there (the manifest of a forked example application, its tsconfig) stay upstream's and are changed by the config-overlay, resource-file or patch layer, while everything the pin does not ship is own code of that directory. That is what lets the overlay of the manifest and the ownership of the directory co-exist, and it is what an application written from scratch needs nothing of: at a pin that ships nothing there, the delta owns the whole directory.
facts.THEIA-APPLICATION-ROOT-IMPL: **Superseded by P5-2 for its second half** (the delta now materializes the application directory; see the fact above). The P5 implementation was: `typeConfig.applicationRoot` is a required field and it is what the type builds its overlay target, its package build and its advisory reader of the application from. The second half of the fact above - the delta *materializing* that directory the way it materializes the own root - is **not** implemented and is not expressible in the contract as it stands: the engine mirrors exactly one own root (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-OWN-ROOT`), and a second mirrored directory is a change of the engine, not of a type. What a product does today instead: it forks one of upstream's example applications, points `applicationRoot` at that directory as it exists **at the pin**, and owns its content through the overlay of its manifest and through resource-file artifacts. An application written from scratch, which exists at no pin, cannot be an overlay target at all (`OVERLAY-BASE-IS-THE-PIN`), and is the open question this fact leaves for the phase that needs it. P5-2 answered exactly that: the engine mirrors every owned directory, and an application that exists at no pin is owned whole.
facts.THEIA-CLEANUP-WHITELIST: The untracked content the fresh pass **keeps**; everything outside the list it removes (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-011#CLEANUP-WHITELIST-CONTENT`): `node_modules/`, `**/lib/` of workspace packages, `**/src-gen/`, `**/gen-esbuild.*.mjs` and `**/gen-webpack*.js` if present, `.eslintcache`, `*.tsbuildinfo`, `.browser_modules/`, `**/.nyc_output/`, `**/coverage/`, `**/dist/` written by the packager the product runs after the build, `plugins/` downloaded by `theia download:plugins` (`02-repository-layout.md`, runtime folders and build outputs). The generated bundler entries are `gen-esbuild.{browser,node,electron}.mjs` since 1.75.0 and the `gen-webpack*` name is the leftover of the build that was removed; the user-editable `esbuild.mjs` of an application is **not** in the list, because a build only regenerates it when it is gone (measured in P5).
facts.THEIA-PACKAGER-OUTPUT: **The packager of the product writes into `<applicationRoot>/dist/`, and that is a build output of the owned application directory.** Upstream has no packager, so no fact of upstream named the directory; the first real consumer of this type ran one after `theia build` (##THEIA-PACKAGE-BUILD) and got 700 MiB of unpacked application, AppImage and archive inside a directory the delta owns. The engine read every file of it as own code the tree had and the delta did not - `status` printed 80-odd `tree-edited` paths and `load` refused with `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` - while `lib/` and `src-gen/` beside it were passed over, because those were named and this was not. `dist/**` therefore joins the build outputs of the application (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-LAYOUT`): the mirror never copies it, `status` never counts it, a plain `load` leaves it where the packager put it, and `load --fresh` removes it - exactly the rule the other outputs of that directory follow. Outside an owned directory the same output is on the cleanup whitelist and survives a fresh pass, as `**/lib/` and `**/src-gen/` do.
facts.THEIA-NATIVE-ADDON-BUILD: **The install of this family compiles a native addon, and its output is on the list too: `dev-packages/ffmpeg/build/`.** Exactly one package of the monorepo carries a `binding.gyp` - `dev-packages/ffmpeg`, the proprietary-codec check of the Electron distribution (`11-release-packaging.md`) - and `npm ci` builds it there through the `node-gyp install` preinstall step (`03-build-watch-lint-test.md`). The directory is untracked, so a fresh pass took it with the rest of the litter; the next bundle of the application then died on `Cannot find module '../build/Debug/ffmpeg.node'` and the only recovery was a full `npm ci`. Measured by the first real consumer of this type on a real clone: 124 untracked paths were removed and this was one of them. The entry names that one package rather than every directory called `build`, because a `build/` anywhere else in this tree is not the output of an install and the discipline of the list is that what is not on it goes away.
facts.THEIA-FORBIDDEN-TARGETS: Never patched: `dev-packages/cli/patches/**` (upstream's own patches of `node_modules`, applied on every install by `theia-patch`), `package-lock.json` (regenerated by install), `src-gen/**` (generated). A patch of `lerna.json` or of the root `package.json` workspace globs is a graft of the constant set and needs a decision record.
facts.THEIA-MARKER-FORMS: Marker comment forms are the engine's by extension; Theia adds none. The SPDX header rule of upstream's lint applies to every `.ts`/`.tsx` under a linted package (PROP-005), which shapes where a marker block may sit in an own file: below the header.
